title: Through holes run a hidden, fixed 1.0 mm past the part bottom, not a parameter and not checked against what is under the part

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
Found while programming a simple 2.5D end-cap plate (user's project) with the CamCraft **v0.19.0** release CLI (macOS arm64), driven headlessly over MCP. Re-checked on upstream main **d00243a5**: **still the same**.

## What happens

`detect_holes` reports a through hole with `"floor_z"` at the part bottom and `"through": true`. At generation the Bore (and Drill/Thread) path then goes a further **1.0 mm** below that floor: the hard-coded `THROUGH_CLEAR = 1.0` in `crates/motion/src/drilling/hole.rs`, passed as `through_allowance` in `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs`.

- The 1.0 mm is not a parameter. It is not shown on the op, in the hole list or in `get_job`, and cannot be changed (the only way is to set `through: false` and type a deeper floor by hand, which is what the user did).
- It is not tied to anything under the part: not the stock bottom, a HAT web, the parallels or the setup. In the repro the part bottom is z 4.826 and the path goes to z 3.826 (the stock bottom is z 0). With the part bottom on the stock bottom, it cuts 1 mm below the stock, into whatever the part sits on, with no note (the fixture laws may catch a modelled parallel; an unmodelled table or spoilboard is not judged).
- It is in mm whatever the document units (an inch user would choose 0.020-0.040 in, and might want it scaled to the tool's tip, e.g. a drill's point length).

## Minimal repro (MCP)

```
import_model   {"path": "End Caps-End capSupport Plate.step", "name": "part"}
move_model     {"name": "part", "position": [0, 37.9, 4.826]}
add_setup      {"name": "Setup 1"}
set_stock      {"box": {"dx": 110, "dy": 185, "dz": 15.33}}
set_wcs        {"stock_point": {"x": "center", "y": "center", "z": "max"}}
add_tool       {"catalog": "EM-0400-2FL", "name": "EM4"}
add_operation  {"kind": "Bore", "tool": "EM4", "name": "Bore", "source": "part", "params": {"stepdown": 2.0}}
detect_holes   {"name": "Bore"}   -> every hole "floor_z": 4.826, "through": true
generate {}                       -> deepest feed z 3.826, no note
```

## Expected

- The break-through is a visible, editable op parameter (default 1.0 mm or a tool-relative value), in document units, saved with the project and settable over MCP.
- The op says what it did (a note: "through holes run 1.0 mm past the part bottom, to z ...").
- The depth past the part is checked against what is under it: never below the stock bottom unless the user allows it, and refused by name if it would reach a fixture.

## Done means

- A through-hole break-through parameter on Drill, Bore and Thread (GUI field, project file, MCP `params`), with a default equal to today's 1.0 mm so existing goldens hold.
- The generated note states the break-through depth; a through hole whose break-through would go below the stock bottom is noted or refused; pinned by tests.

Related: #1556 (large bores in hole detection).
